references.text: This is the same verse in other numbering systems (Leviticus 6:5 in some Bibles), which deals with restitution plus an added fifth.
Describes a similar principle of restitution plus an added fifth for guilt offerings concerning holy things.
Same principle of adding a fifth when making restitution for holy gifts that were eaten by mistake.
Repeated principle of adding a fifth when redeeming vows and property.
Describes full restitution plus an added fifth for sin committed against another person.
Basic laws regarding responsibility for stolen or entrusted goods that form the background for the principle of restitution.
Ezekiel describes how the wicked must restore what they have stolen as part of repentance.
Zacchaeus promises to give back fourfold to those he has defrauded, illustrating the principle of restitution in practice.
